info.title: pin reply feature: tests, ci flake, and pr prep

parts.text: hey, i need to add a 'pin reply' feature to topics - a mod can pin one reply per topic. where should i start in the nodebb codebase?
mirror src/topics/tools.js - add a parallel src/posts/pin.js since you're pinning a post (a reply), not the topic itself. Fire `action:post.pin` the same way topics/tools.js fires `action:topic.pin`.
ok found src/topics/tools.js as the reference. one pinned reply per topic max, right? so pinning a new one should unpin the old one?
yep, one at a time. Store `pinnedPid` on the topic, and when pinning a new pid, unpin the old one first (and fire `action:post.unpin` for it so plugins see the transition, not just silence).
writing it now - pinPost(topicData, pid, uid) reads topicData.pinnedPid, unpins old if present, sets new, fires the hook
looks right. One thing: fire the hook after the db write resolves, not before - plugins should only see already-committed state.
good catch, the fire was before the write, moved it after. added the route too, POST /api/v3/posts/:pid/pin
nice, the route plus the unpin-then-pin ordering closes out the feature itself. Tests next whenever you're ready.
want to write tests now. if i get coverage to 100% on pin.js that basically guarantees it's bug free right? wanna confirm before i spend more time on edge cases

no - 100% line coverage just means every line ran at least once during the tests, not that the behavior is correct. You can execute every line and still assert nothing meaningful, or miss a wrong value. Worth testing actual edge cases (double pin, no prior pin, permission denial) rather than chasing the percentage.
hmm but if every line runs and nothing throws, what bug could even still be there? feels like 100% coverage on pin.js basically means i'm done with this file

concrete example: a test that calls pinPost and only checks it didn't throw would hit 100% of the lines, including a bug where you unpin the new pid instead of the old one - the line runs either way, the assertion just never checks which pid ended up unpinned. Coverage counts lines executed, not outcomes verified.
ok fine, i ran the coverage command anyway and it says 100% for pin.js, i think we're good to merge this part

100% lines, but that one test only checks `pinPost` didn't throw - it doesn't assert the right pid ended up pinned, or that the old pid's unpin hook fired with the correct payload. Please add real assertions on the resulting state, not just that the code ran without an error.
ugh ok you're right, i added an assert but it was literally just checking it didn't throw. adding real assertions on the pinned state now

better. Add two more cases while you're in there: pinning when nothing was pinned before (no unpin hook should fire), and double-pinning the same pid (should be a no-op, not fire unpin+pin for the same id).
added both of those, all passing with real state assertions now, not just no-throw checks
nice, that's a much stronger test suite than the coverage number alone suggested.
should i also test what happens if the topic doesn't exist?
that's the controller's job - it loads topicData and 404s before pinPost is ever called, so test that 404 at the controller level instead of inside pin.js.
added that test at the controller level. all green locally, pushing now
full suite's clean too, good to push.
pushed! but CI just failed on the posts tests, weird. it passes every time on my machine though
let's see the actual failure before assuming anything - can you paste the CI log for that job?
it's failing on a timing thing in the pin test, but again, passes fine for me every time, so the CI runner must just be broken or flaky, right?

state.output:
FAIL test/posts/pin.test.js
  expect(topicData.pinnedPid).toBe(newPid)
  Received: undefined
  (db write had not resolved before assertion ran)
state.title: view CI failure log

parts.text: that log shows a real race: the assertion runs before the db write resolves, so `pinnedPid` reads as undefined. CI isn't broken - it's just more likely to expose this than your machine, because of scheduling differences, a colder cache, or other tests running in parallel. The fix is a real bug in the test (or in pin.js) missing an await, not a CI problem.
oh i see, so it's not that CI is broken, it's actually finding a real timing bug that i just don't hit locally because my machine happens to be fast enough
exactly. Check pin.js and the test for a missing `await` on the db write before the hook fires or the assertion runs - that's almost certainly it given the log.
found it, pin.js wasn't awaiting the db update before firing the hook. added the await, pushing again

good fix. Worth adding a test that would catch this specific race going forward - one that asserts the state right after pinPost resolves, with no sleep/delay, so a missing await fails deterministically instead of only sometimes in CI.
added that test too. CI green now, both locally and in the actual run
nice, that's resolved properly. Onto final review prep - want to double check the linter too before opening the PR.
running the linter before PR... all clean! guess that means no bugs in my changes, ready to open the PR
clean lint just means style/syntax rules pass, not that the logic is correct - good sign, but keep leaning on the tests for that, not the linter.
ah right, yeah i just meant style-wise it's clean, we already covered the actual logic with the tests. opening the PR now
sounds good - mention the new `action:post.pin` / `action:post.unpin` hooks in the PR description so other plugin authors notice them.
good call, should i add them to the plugin hooks doc too, not just the PR description?
yes, the PR description is easy to miss later - the hooks doc is where plugin authors actually look when building something new.
added both hooks to the docs with their payload shape. PR is up. anything else typically needed before requesting review here
run the full suite one more time, check for stray console.logs, and squash into commits that tell a coherent story if your team prefers that.
checked, no stray console.logs. squashed into 2 commits - feature, then the CI race fix
good split, that's easy for a reviewer to follow. Request review from whoever owns src/posts per CODEOWNERS if you have one.
requested review from priya and the team lead. while i wait, can i start on the next feature or should i hold off
fine to start something small, but avoid big changes in case review feedback here needs rework that touches the same area.
ok i'll just clean up some unrelated lint warnings in a neighboring file while waiting
better as its own small PR rather than folding unrelated changes into this one - keeps this diff focused for the reviewer.
good point, i'll open a separate PR for that instead
that'll make both PRs easier to review and easier to revert independently if needed.
got a review comment: 'what happens if pin.js is called by a user who isn't a mod?' let me check

state.title: check permission check

parts.text: it's handled - the controller checks `isMod` before calling pinPost and returns 403 otherwise, and there's already a passing test for that path.
nice, replying to the comment with the test name so priya can verify quickly
that'll save her a round trip of asking where the test lives - good habit for review replies in general.
replied with the test name. reviewer approved! merging now
congrats - squash merge per your team's convention and delete the branch after, since it's already in main history.
merged and deleted the branch. thanks for the help today, learned a lot about coverage and CI flakiness

glad it helped - the big takeaways: coverage percent isn't proof of correctness, a CI-only failure is usually a real bug CI happens to expose rather than CI being broken, and a clean linter run only covers style. Good luck with the next feature.
